name: Sihon and Og
charge: Refusing Israel passage on the king’s highway and coming out to battle against them
summary: Israel was forbidden to meddle with Esau, Moab or Ammon, for the Most High had appointed their possessions. To Sihon king of the Amorites Moses sent words of peace: only pass through on the highway, buying meat and water for money. The Lord hardened his spirit as He had hardened Pharaoh’s, that He might deliver him into Israel’s hand, for the Amorites’ iniquity was full. Og, of the remnant of giants, came out after him. Both kingdoms were utterly destroyed, and the land east of Jordan became the first inheritance.
offenseFull: Israel had compassed mount Seir long enough, and was charged to turn northward and pass through the coast of their brethren the children of Esau, the people called the white man today, and not meddle with them, for mount Seir was given to Esau for a possession and not so much as a foot breadth of it was Israel’s; and the same for Moab and Ammon, the children of Lot, whose lands the Most High had appointed (Deuteronomy 2:2-9, 19). Then the word changed: they were to rise up and pass over the river Arnon, for the Lord had given Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land into their hand, and that day He would begin to put the dread and the fear of Israel on the nations under the whole heaven, so that they would tremble and be in anguish (Deuteronomy 2:24-25).

Moses sent messengers to Sihon with words of peace: let Israel pass through his land along the highway, turning neither to the right hand nor to the left, buying meat and water for money, only passing through on foot, exactly as they had passed the children of Esau in Seir and the Moabites in Ar (Deuteronomy 2:26-29; Numbers 21:21-22). But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let them pass, for the Lord their God hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate so that He might deliver him into their hand: the same dealing as with Pharaoh, the heart hardened so the judgment could land, for the iniquity of the Amorites was full and their land was appointed to Israel (Deuteronomy 2:30; Genesis 15:16). He gathered all his people, went out against Israel into the wilderness, and fought at Jahaz (Numbers 21:23). Then Og the king of Bashan came out against them with all his people at Edrei (Deuteronomy 3:1). Og was an Amorite, and the Amorite came of Canaan the son of Ham (Genesis 10:6, 16); the Hamitic nations were known for great stature, which is why the tallest peoples on the earth to this day are of that line. He remained of the remnant of giants, and his bedstead of iron was nine cubits long and four broad, about thirteen feet by six, near the size of two king beds set together (Deuteronomy 3:11).
judgmentFull: The Lord delivered Sihon before Israel, and they smote him, his sons and all his people, took all his cities at that time, and utterly destroyed the men, women and little ones of every city, leaving none to remain; only the cattle and the spoil of the cities they took as a prey for themselves (Deuteronomy 2:33-35; Numbers 21:24-26). That is how thorough the judgment of the Most High was for Israel’s sake, and how privileged this people was, and still they struggled to believe Him. Of Og the Lord said not to fear him, for He had delivered him and all his people and his land into their hand; so they smote him, his sons and all his people until none was left alive, and possessed his land (Numbers 21:33-35). Threescore cities were taken, all fenced with high walls, gates and bars, beside a great many unwalled towns, and not one was left (Deuteronomy 3:4-6).

The giants were famous from the beginning, of great stature and expert in war, yet the Lord chose them not and gave them no way of knowledge; they were destroyed because they had no wisdom and perished through their own foolishness (Baruch 3:26-28). From Aroer by the brink of the river Arnon to Gilead there was not one city too strong for them, and the Lord delivered all of it; only they did not come to the land of the children of Ammon, nor to anything

the Lord their God had forbidden (Deuteronomy 2:36-37). And when it was over, the people did not boast in their own swords: they said that the Lord their God delivered the king of Bashan into their hands (Deuteronomy 3:3). Always remember that the battle is the Lord’s, and that this fight is spiritual; Israel needs no weapons of mass destruction, because the Bible is the weapon, and when the commandments are kept the Most High fights for His people. Joshua was made to look at these two kings and told that so the Lord would do to all the kingdoms he passed into, so he was not to fear them (Deuteronomy 3:21-22). The psalm keeps the record: He smote great kings, Sihon king of the Amorites and Og the king of Bashan, and gave their land as a heritage to Israel His servant, for His mercy lasts for ever (Psalms 136:17-22).

text.text: And the Lord spake unto me, saying,
Ye have compassed this mountain long enough: turn you northward.

And command thou the people, saying, Ye are to pass through the coast of your brethren the children of Esau, which dwell in Seir; and they shall be afraid of you: take ye good heed unto yourselves therefore:
Meddle not with them; for I will not give you of their land, no, not so much as a foot breadth; because I have given mount Seir unto Esau for a possession.
Ye shall buy meat of them for money, that ye may eat; and ye shall also buy water of them for money, that ye may drink.

For the Lord thy God hath blessed thee in all the works of thy hand: he knoweth thy walking through this great wilderness: these forty years the Lord thy God hath been with thee; thou hast lacked nothing.

And when we passed by from our brethren the children of Esau, which dwelt in Seir, through the way of the plain from Elath, and from Ezion–gaber, we turned and passed by the way of the wilderness of Moab.

And the Lord said unto me, Distress not the Moabites, neither contend with them in battle: for I will not give thee of their land for a possession; because I have given Ar unto the children of Lot for a possession.

And when thou comest nigh over against the children of Ammon, distress them not, nor meddle with them: for I will not give thee of the land of the children of Ammon any possession; because I have given it unto the children of Lot for a possession.

Rise ye up, take your journey, and pass over the river Arnon: behold, I have given into thine hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land: begin to possess it, and contend with him in battle.

This day will I begin to put the dread of thee and the fear of thee upon the nations that are under the whole heaven, who shall hear report of thee, and shall tremble, and be in anguish because of thee.
And I sent messengers out of the wilderness of Kedemoth unto Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace, saying,
Let me pass through thy land: I will go along by the high way, I will neither turn unto the right hand nor to the left.
Thou shalt sell me meat for money, that I may eat; and give me water for money, that I may drink: only I will pass through on my feet;
(As the children of Esau which dwell in Seir, and the Moabites which dwell in Ar, did unto me;) until I shall pass over Jordan into the land which the Lord our God giveth us.
And Israel sent messengers unto Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,

Let me pass through thy land: we will not turn into the fields, or into the vineyards; we will not drink of the waters of the well: but we will go along by the king’s high way, until we be past thy borders.
But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass by him: for the Lord thy God hardened his spirit, and made his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into thy hand, as appeareth this day.
But in the fourth generation they shall come hither again: for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.

And Sihon would not suffer Israel to pass through his border: but Sihon gathered all his people together, and went out against Israel into the wilderness: and he came to Jahaz, and fought against Israel.
Then we turned, and went up the way to Bashan: and Og the king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.
And the sons of Ham; Cush, and Mizraim, and Phut, and Canaan.
And the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgasite,

For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants; behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron; is it not in Rabbath of the children of Ammon? nine cubits was the length thereof, and four cubits the breadth of it, after the cubit of a man.
And the Lord our God delivered him before us; and we smote him, and his sons, and all his people.
And we took all his cities at that time, and utterly destroyed the men, and the women, and the little ones, of every city, we left none to remain:
Only the cattle we took for a prey unto ourselves, and the spoil of the cities which we took.
And Israel smote him with the edge of the sword, and possessed his land from Arnon unto Jabbok, even unto the children of Ammon: for the border of the children of Ammon was strong.
And Israel took all these cities: and Israel dwelt in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon, and in all the villages thereof.
For Heshbon was the city of Sihon the king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab, and taken all his land out of his hand, even unto Arnon.
And they turned and went up by the way of Bashan: and Og the king of Bashan went out against them, he, and all his people, to the battle at Edrei.

And the Lord said unto Moses, Fear him not: for I have delivered him into thy hand, and all his people, and his land; and thou shalt do to him as thou didst unto Sihon king of the Amorites, which dwelt at Heshbon.
So they smote him, and his sons, and all his people, until there was none left him alive: and they possessed his land.
And we took all his cities at that time, there was not a city which we took not from them, threescore cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
All these cities were fenced with high walls, gates, and bars; beside unwalled towns a great many.
And we utterly destroyed them, as we did unto Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying the men, women, and children, of every city.
There were the giants famous from the beginning, that were of so great stature, and so expert in war.
Those did not the Lord choose, neither gave he the way of knowledge unto them:
But they were destroyed, because they had no wisdom, and perished through their own foolishness.
From Aroer, which is by the brink of the river of Arnon, and from the city that is by the river, even unto Gilead, there was not one city too strong for us: the Lord our God delivered all unto us:
Only unto the land of the children of Ammon thou camest not, nor unto any place of the river Jabbok, nor unto the cities in the mountains, nor unto whatsoever the Lord our God forbad us.
So the Lord our God delivered into our hands Og also, the king of Bashan, and all his people: and we smote him until none was left to him remaining.
And I commanded Joshua at that time, saying, Thine eyes have seen all that the Lord your God hath done unto these two kings: so shall the Lord do unto all the kingdoms whither thou passest.
Ye shall not fear them: for the Lord your God he shall fight for you.
To him which smote great kings: for his mercy endureth for ever:
And slew famous kings: for his mercy endureth for ever:
Sihon king of the Amorites: for his mercy endureth for ever:
And Og the king of Bashan: for his mercy endureth for ever:
And gave their land for an heritage: for his mercy endureth for ever:
Even an heritage unto Israel his servant: for his mercy endureth for ever.
